evidence: Changes offload plugin launch sizing, far from MemorySSA and LLVM scalar optimizer invalidation.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Refactors offload plugin block-limit computation to depend on the kernel’s requested thread count instead of using a fixed device-wide maximum. The generic device interface changes getBlockLimit into a virtual method taking NumThreads, and AMDGPU overrides it to derive a block cap from the product of max teams and thread limit divided by the per-block thread count, with saturation to uint32_t. Kernel launch sizing now clamps both explicit user block counts and preferred block counts against this thread-dependent limit.
Mechanisms: launch configuration sizing; thread-count-dependent block limit calculation; device-specific override of generic policy; clamping user/preferred block counts to device limits
Touched symbols: GenericDeviceTy::getBlockLimit; AMDGPUDeviceTy::getBlockLimit; GenericKernelTy::getEffectiveNumBlocks; GridValues.GV_Max_Teams; getThreadLimit
Risk relevance: Changes kernel launch bookkeeping and resource sizing, which can indirectly affect optimizer assumptions and runtime behavior; Introduces a new virtual interface contract for block-limit queries, increasing the chance of mismatched callers or overrides; AMDGPU-specific arithmetic on launch limits may expose overflow or edge-case regressions for unusual thread counts
Build risk: Touches common plugin interface headers and implementation code, so it can affect multiple offload backends; Requires all callers to pass EffectiveNumThreads, increasing compile-time coupling and potential API breakage; Behavioral change is test-sensitive because it alters launch sizing semantics rather than just internal refactoring
